description: Deterministic, generated calibration signals (pure tone + linear chirp) used to drive a real output device in CI and assert on what a real capture round trip actually recorded — not just that buffers arrived. Feeds the fixture-player binary and the strict live-audio-smoke signal assertions (feature `live-audio-smoke`).

notes: Every sample is produced by a closed-form function of (frequency, amplitude, duration, sample_rate) — no RNG, no recording, no third-party dataset.
The validator (src-tauri/src/audio_signal_fixtures.rs) regenerates any missing WAV and asserts the regenerated bytes are byte-for-byte identical to the checked-in file.
Recomposed at test time from the existing checked-in source_separation component WAVs — no new recording, no new dataset.

Mirrors the segment timing of source_separation's own two-speaker-turn-taking-001 fixture (speaker A 0-3000ms, 400ms gap, speaker B 3400-6400ms, 400ms trailing gap 6400-6800ms) for a well-understood, already-reviewed shape.

audio-graph-1ee3/653a: added the 6400-6800ms trailing silence gap after speaker B, mirroring the proven-sufficient 400ms A/B gap (that gap is exactly what already lets Deepgram's own in-stream endpointing finalize speaker A live — a_words=7 in the 2026-08-20 protected-provider-smoke run). Speaker B was the LAST audio in the file before this change, so it had no same-stream silence cue to finalize on and no chance to be flushed before the client's own Stop-path abandons the read side (audio-graph-653a: run_io's AudioCmd::Stop arm sends the close frame and returns immediately, never reading whatever Deepgram sends back). This gives B the identical in-stream cue A already gets, entirely during normal audio delivery and before disconnect() is ever reached — independent of whether 653a's close-path defect gets fixed.

attribution.citation: Panayotov, V., Chen, G., Povey, D., and Khudanpur, S. LibriSpeech: an ASR corpus based on public domain audio books. ICASSP 2015.

expected_signal._rms_floor_note: The strict live-audio-smoke test measures RMS over a 2500ms window at an arbitrary phase of this looping fixture, not the whole-file RMS. Computed the circular 2.5s-window RMS across every 50ms-offset alignment of the checked-in WAV: min 818.55 (at offset ~1.10s, inside speaker A's low-energy opening plus the silence gap). 600.0 sits comfortably below that worst case (leaving ~27% margin) while staying far above silence (RMS 0), so the floor still fails a captured-silence run without spuriously failing a healthy one at an unlucky loop phase. Re-verified after audio-graph-1ee3/653a extended the loop to 6800ms (added a 400ms trailing silence gap after speaker B, 6400-6800ms): the global worst-case window is UNCHANGED at 818.55/1.10s — the new trailing-silence region's own worst window (912.99 at offset ~6.40s, wrapping partway into speaker A's next loop iteration) is higher than the pre-existing worst case, so 600.0 remains a valid floor with no numeric change needed.
